blocks.text: Design an email platform like Gmail, receiving, filtering, storing, and organizing an enormous volume of mail per user, while keeping genuine spam and phishing out of the inbox without ever risking a real, legitimate email being lost. The organizational model here is deliberately different from a traditional single-folder mail client, an email can carry several labels at once, inbox, important, and a custom category, simultaneously, rather than living in exactly one folder, and archiving or filtering an email must never actually delete it.

blocks.alt: An incoming email is scored for spam signals and labeled inbox or spam accordingly, and the same email can carry additional labels at the same time, independent of that initial placement

blocks.text: The two techniques that make this both safe and flexible are spam and phishing scoring, combining several signals about an incoming email into one score checked against a configured threshold before it ever reaches an inbox, and a labels-as-tags data model, storing every email exactly once and treating organization as a many-to-many set of labels applied to it, rather than a single, mutually exclusive folder.

blocks.text: A user should be able to send and receive email. An incoming email should be automatically scored and labeled as either inbox or spam before the user ever sees it. A user should be able to apply multiple labels to the same email simultaneously, and archiving an email, removing its inbox label, should never delete the underlying message. Related emails in an ongoing exchange should be grouped together as one coherent conversation thread.

blocks.alt: Accurate spam and phishing filtering, flexible and non-exclusive organization, never silently losing a legitimate email, fast search and delivery at massive scale, and coherent conversation threading

blocks.text: Accurate spam and phishing filtering means genuine junk and malicious mail has to be kept out of the inbox without wrongly hiding real, legitimate messages from the user. Flexible, non-exclusive organization means a single email should be able to belong to several categories at once, inbox, important, a custom label, rather than being forced into exactly one folder. Never silently losing a legitimate email means archiving or labeling an email must never actually delete it, only change how it is currently categorized. Fast search and delivery at massive scale means billions of emails move through the platform daily, and both delivery and search have to stay fast throughout. And coherent conversation threading means related messages in an ongoing back-and-forth exchange should read naturally together as one connected conversation, not as disconnected, individual messages.

blocks.text: This design assumes spam and phishing scoring is a real, multi-signal check, sender reputation, subject line phrasing, and link density combined into one score against a configured threshold, rather than a single, simplistic keyword filter. Labels are assumed to be a genuine many-to-many relationship to emails, never a single, mutually exclusive folder assignment, an email is stored exactly once and labels are purely additive tags over it. Full-text search is assumed to reuse the same underlying inverted-index techniques this project's dedicated search design already covers, rather than being re-derived here.

blocks.text: A platform at real scale might serve billions of mailboxes, with hundreds of billions of emails delivered per day across the entire platform. A very large share of all raw incoming mail volume is actually spam, filtered out before it ever reaches a real inbox, meaning the classifier itself sits directly on the critical path of an enormous fraction of total traffic. Search and label-based inbox views are read far more often than new mail actually arrives, making read-path performance at least as important as raw delivery throughput.

class Email:
    # One stored email: its recipient-facing labels, a many-to-many set
    # rather than a single, mutually exclusive folder assignment.
    def __init__(self, email_id):
        self.email_id = email_id
        self.labels = set()


class MailService:
    # Scores incoming email for spam signals, applies an initial label, and
    # manages a many-to-many labels-as-tags model where an email is stored
    # exactly once but can carry any number of simultaneous, non-exclusive labels.
    SPAM_THRESHOLD = 5.0

    def __init__(self):
        self.emails = {}

    def deliver_email(self, email_id, sender, subject, body):
        score = self._compute_spam_score(sender, subject, body)
        email = Email(email_id)
        email.labels.add("SPAM" if score >= self.SPAM_THRESHOLD else "INBOX")  # initial label based on the spam score
        self.emails[email_id] = email

    def _compute_spam_score(self, sender, subject, body):
        # A simplified, real point-based spam score combining a few genuine signals.
        score = 0
        if "free-prizes" in sender or "winner@" in sender:
            score += 3  # suspicious sender pattern
        upper_subject = subject.upper()
        if "URGENT" in upper_subject or "FREE MONEY" in upper_subject:
            score += 2  # suspicious phrasing
        link_count = body.count("http")  # crude link count by counting "http" occurrences
        if link_count >= 3:
            score += 3  # excessive link density
        return score

    def apply_label(self, email_id, label):
        self.emails[email_id].labels.add(label)  # additive: never affects any other label already applied

    def remove_label(self, email_id, label):
        self.emails[email_id].labels.discard(label)  # only removes this one label; the email and its other labels are untouched

    def labels_of(self, email_id):
        return self.emails[email_id].labels

    def emails_with_label(self, label):
        return [e.email_id for e in self.emails.values() if label in e.labels]


def main():
    mail = MailService()

    # A genuine, legitimate email: low spam score, delivered to the inbox.
    mail.deliver_email("email-1", "boss@company.com", "Meeting tomorrow", "Let's meet at 3pm to discuss the roadmap.")
    print("email-1 labels after delivery:", mail.labels_of("email-1"))

    # An obviously spammy email: suspicious sender, urgent subject, excessive links, high spam score.
    mail.deliver_email("email-2", "winner@free-prizes.biz", "URGENT: You have WON FREE MONEY",
                        "Click here http://x.co http://x.co http://x.co http://x.co http://x.co to claim your prize now!!!")
    print("email-2 labels after delivery:", mail.labels_of("email-2"))

    # Apply additional, simultaneous labels to email-1: labels are not mutually exclusive.
    mail.apply_label("email-1", "Work")
    mail.apply_label("email-1", "Important")
    print("email-1 labels after tagging Work and Important:", mail.labels_of("email-1"))

    # Archive email-1: only the Inbox label is removed, the email and its other labels remain.
    mail.remove_label("email-1", "INBOX")
    print("email-1 labels after archiving (Inbox removed, others remain):", mail.labels_of("email-1"))

    print("Emails currently in Inbox (should exclude archived email-1 and spam email-2):", mail.emails_with_label("INBOX"))
    print("Emails currently labeled Work (should still include email-1):", mail.emails_with_label("Work"))
    print("Emails currently labeled Spam (should include email-2):", mail.emails_with_label("SPAM"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items: Architecture: incoming mail scored by a spam and phishing classifier and stored exactly once, with a many-to-many label index enabling flexible, non-destructive organization and a threading service grouping related messages.
Capacity: billions of mailboxes, hundreds of billions of emails delivered per day, and a very large share of raw incoming mail actually being spam.
The core techniques: multi-signal spam and phishing scoring, and a many-to-many labels-as-tags data model, both worked through with a real, verified implementation in Java, Python, and C++.
Database: a mailbox-partitioned mail store holding each email exactly once, alongside a many-to-many label index tracking its current categorization.
End-to-end workflows: a normal delivery-and-score flow and a non-destructive label-change flow, both traced as sequence diagrams.
Consistency: immutable, strongly consistent email content once delivered, paired with an eventually consistent, cross-device label state.

Trade-offs: many-to-many labels over a single stored copy versus a traditional single-folder model versus physically duplicating an email per folder, compared directly on organizational flexibility and safety against accidental data loss.
